findings.issue_text: [High/security] Backup code comparison uses Array.indexOf on decrypted codes, which is not constant-time; use a timing-safe compare (next-auth-options.ts:150)
[High/security] If a user supplies both a TOTP code and a backup code, the TOTP path is silently skipped when backupCode is present (next-auth-options.ts:150)

[Medium/concurrency] Backup code single-use enforcement is read-modify-write with no transaction/locking; two concurrent logins with the same code can both succeed — use a transaction or compare-and-swap update (next-auth-options.ts:145-158)

[Medium/security] symmetricEncrypt uses CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY without checking it exists; if unset, secrets are encrypted with an undefined key and stored unrecoverably — add the same guard used elsewhere (totp/setup.ts:60-66)
[Medium/bug] req.body.backupCode used without type validation; a non-string value will make replaceAll throw, producing a 500 instead of a 400 — validate typeof === string (totp/disable.ts:55)

[Medium/bug] JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) on stored backup codes is unguarded; corrupt/legacy data throws an unhandled 500 instead of returning MissingBackupCodes/InternalServerError (totp/disable.ts:56)

[Medium/bug] Modal can be dismissed at DisplayBackupCodes step via backdrop/escape, skipping onEnable(); user ends up with stored backup codes but 2FA never enabled and codes never shown again (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:92-97)
[Medium/bug] Re-submitting the password step calls setup again and regenerates/overwrites backup codes, silently invalidating codes the user already copied/downloaded (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:95)
[Medium/bug] backupCodesUrl blob URL is never revoked on modal close/unmount, leaking the object URL across modal lifecycles (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:99)

[Low/bug] minLength/maxLength of 10/11 don't enforce the XXXXX-XXXXX pattern; an 11-char input without a dash passes HTML validation but fails server verification — use a pattern or normalize-on-input (BackupCode.tsx:20-23)

[Low/bug] If the disable request fails with a network error after the server consumed the backup code, retry semantics are unclear; resetForm only runs on the 200 path (DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:58-63)

[Medium/test_gap] No e2e tests for logging in with a backup code, single-use enforcement, incorrect backup code error path, or disabling 2FA with a backup code — security-critical paths should be tested (login.2fa.e2e.ts)

[Low/api] disable always sends backupCode (possibly empty string); server distinguishes backup vs TOTP on truthiness, so an empty-string value could unexpectedly trigger the backup path — send null/omit when empty (TwoFactorAuthAPI.ts:22)

[Low/bug] If a twoFactorEnabled user submits backupCode but has no stored codes, MissingBackupCodes is returned even when a valid totpCode is present; consider falling through or making the modal mutually exclusive server-side (totp/disable.ts:50-52)

[Low/doc_defect] backup_code_instructions about single-use consumption is reused as the dialog description for the DisplayBackupCodes step; a save-this-now message would be more appropriate (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx)

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] Backup code comparison uses Array.indexOf on decrypted codes, which is not constant-time; use a timing-safe compare (next-auth-options.ts:150)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code verification does `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, which relies on normal JS string equality and `Array#indexOf` (not timing-safe). This is a valid security-hardening concern, but the diff does not establish an actual exploitable vulnerability/severity in practice (remote timing attacks over network are typically noisy), so it reads more as a best-practice improvement than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] If a user supplies both a TOTP code and a backup code, the TOTP path is silently skipped when backupCode is present (next-auth-options.ts:150)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the 2FA logic is `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode) { ... } else if (user.twoFactorEnabled) { ... totp ... }`. This means that when `backupCode` is present, the TOTP verification branch is not executed at all, even if `credentials.totpCode` is also provided. As a result, a request supplying both factors will be evaluated only as a backup-code attempt; if the backup code is wrong/used but the TOTP is correct, login will still fail with `IncorrectBackupCode`. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior issue introduced by the new branching order (backup-code path takes precedence).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] Backup code single-use enforcement is read-modify-write with no transaction/locking; two concurrent logins with the same code can both succeed — use a transaction or compare-and-swap update (next-auth-options.ts:145-158)
matched_golden_ids: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same race condition: backup codes are checked and then updated via a non-atomic read/modify/write, so two concurrent logins using the same backup code can both pass validation and mark it used, effectively allowing a one-time code to be accepted multiple times without locking/transactional update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] symmetricEncrypt uses CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY without checking it exists; if unset, secrets are encrypted with an undefined key and stored unrecoverably — add the same guard used elsewhere (totp/setup.ts:60-66)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the diff adds `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` (and still encrypts `twoFactorSecret` the same way) without any check that `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set. Elsewhere in this diff (e.g. `totp/disable.ts` and `next-auth-options.ts`) there is an explicit guard that errors when the key is missing. Without a guard here, the setup endpoint could encrypt/store data with an undefined key (or throw unpredictably), leading to unrecoverable 2FA secrets/backup codes or broken setup behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] req.body.backupCode used without type validation; a non-string value will make replaceAll throw, producing a 500 instead of a 400 — validate typeof === string (totp/disable.ts:55)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the backup-code branch checks only truthiness (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)`) and then calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If a client sends a non-string JSON value for `backupCode` (e.g., number/object/array), `replaceAll` will throw at runtime, resulting in a 500 instead of a controlled 400 error. The diff shows no `typeof req.body.backupCode === "string"` guard or schema validation in this handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) on stored backup codes is unguarded; corrupt/legacy data throws an unhandled 500 instead of returning MissingBackupCodes/InternalServerError (totp/disable.ts:56)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode`, the code does `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY));` with no guarding. If `user.backupCodes` is corrupt, legacy/non-JSON, or decryption yields invalid JSON, `JSON.parse` will throw and the handler will error out (500) rather than returning a controlled `{ error: MissingBackupCodes }` / `{ error: InternalServerError }` response. The diff shows no try/catch around this parse/decrypt path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] Modal can be dismissed at DisplayBackupCodes step via backdrop/escape, skipping onEnable(); user ends up with stored backup codes but 2FA never enabled and codes never shown again (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:92-97)

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, after a successful enable response, the code no longer calls `onEnable()` (it does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and returns). The only place that calls `onEnable()` is the explicit “close” button shown in the DisplayBackupCodes step. There is no handling in `onOpenChange` to call `onEnable()`/`resetState()` when the dialog is dismissed via other means (e.g., backdrop/escape), and the cancel button is intentionally hidden for that step. So it’s possible to close the modal at DisplayBackupCodes without running `onEnable()`, leaving the parent/UI not updated. (The finding’s claim that “2FA never enabled” is overstated—server-side enable likely already succeeded—but the skipped callback/UI state issue is real.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] Re-submitting the password step calls setup again and regenerates/overwrites backup codes, silently invalidating codes the user already copied/downloaded (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:95)

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, backup codes are generated during `handleSetup` (password step) and stored in component state, but they are not displayed/copyable/downloadable until the later `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` step (after `handleEnable` succeeds and `setStep(DisplayBackupCodes)` runs). Once on `DisplayBackupCodes`, the password-step `<form onSubmit={handleSetup}>` is no longer rendered, so the user can’t “re-submit the password step” while already having copied/downloaded codes. While repeated setup submissions could regenerate codes/secret on the server, the claim that it would silently invalidate codes the user already copied/downloaded is not supported by the shown UI flow in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] backupCodesUrl blob URL is never revoked on modal close/unmount, leaking the object URL across modal lifecycles (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:99)
matched_golden_ids: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags that the backupCodesUrl blob/object URL is never revoked on modal close/unmount, causing a leak across lifecycles. This is the same underlying problem as the golden comment about not revoking the object URL on component unmount leading to a memory leak.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] minLength/maxLength of 10/11 don't enforce the XXXXX-XXXXX pattern; an 11-char input without a dash passes HTML validation but fails server verification — use a pattern or normalize-on-input (BackupCode.tsx:20-23)

adjudication.rationale: In `BackupCode.tsx`, the input only uses `minLength={10}` and `maxLength={11}` with a placeholder `"XXXXX-XXXXX"`, but no `pattern`/input normalization is applied. This allows an 11-character value without a dash (e.g. `XXXXXXXXXXX`) to satisfy HTML length constraints while the server-side check in both `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `next-auth-options.ts` compares `backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` against stored 10-char codes, causing such inputs to fail verification despite passing client validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] If the disable request fails with a network error after the server consumed the backup code, retry semantics are unclear; resetForm only runs on the 200 path (DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:58-63)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `resetForm()` is only called on the `response.status === 200` path in `DisableTwoFactorModal` (after `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(...)`). However, the claim that a network error could occur “after the server consumed the backup code” leading to unclear retry semantics isn’t supported by the disable API code shown: in `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` the backup code is only checked for membership and not individually consumed/removed there (it’s only cleared when 2FA is successfully disabled via `backupCodes: null`), and the diff doesn’t show any server behavior that would make a retry fail or behave ambiguously. The finding is therefore largely speculative beyond what the diff verifies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No e2e tests for logging in with a backup code, single-use enforcement, incorrect backup code error path, or disabling 2FA with a backup code — security-critical paths should be tested (login.2fa.e2e.ts)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new backup-code authentication and 2FA-disable flows (e.g., `credentials.backupCode` handling in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code branch in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, UI toggle to `BackupCode` in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` and `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx`). However, the only e2e test updates in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` cover displaying/copying/downloading backup codes after enabling 2FA, and even include a TODO to add more backup code tests. There are no e2e tests for login with a backup code, incorrect/missing backup code error paths, single-use enforcement, or disabling 2FA using a backup code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] disable always sends backupCode (possibly empty string); server distinguishes backup vs TOTP on truthiness, so an empty-string value could unexpectedly trigger the backup path — send null/omit when empty (TwoFactorAuthAPI.ts:22)

adjudication.rationale: In the disable API handler, the backup-code branch is gated by truthiness: `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)`. An empty string is falsy in JS, so sending `backupCode: ""` will *not* trigger the backup-code path; it will fall through to the TOTP branch (`else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)`). Also, if `backupCode` is `undefined`, `JSON.stringify({ password, code, backupCode })` omits the key entirely. Therefore the stated risk that an empty-string value could unexpectedly trigger the backup path is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] If a twoFactorEnabled user submits backupCode but has no stored codes, MissingBackupCodes is returned even when a valid totpCode is present; consider falling through or making the modal mutually exclusive server-side (totp/disable.ts:50-52)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` takes precedence over the TOTP path (`else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)`). If a request includes a non-empty `backupCode`, the handler will return `MissingBackupCodes` when `user.backupCodes` is null, even if `req.body.code` (TOTP) is also present and valid—there is no fall-through to TOTP verification in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] backup_code_instructions about single-use consumption is reused as the dialog description for the DisplayBackupCodes step; a save-this-now message would be more appropriate (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx)

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the new SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes uses `setupDescriptions[SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes] = t("backup_code_instructions")`, and `DialogContent` always renders `description={setupDescriptions[step]}`. The `backup_code_instructions` string ("Each backup code can be used exactly once...") is thus shown as the description while displaying the actual backup codes, which is a UX/content mismatch (a “save/copy/download these now” message would better fit). This is not a functional defect, but it is a specific, diff-grounded documentation/UX issue.
